summary: A game loop repeats three steps every frame: update positions, check collisions, and draw. In Swing, a javax.swing.Timer runs the loop and repaint() asks for a new frame.
notes: new Timer(FRAME_MS, e -> gameLoop()).start() runs gameLoop every 16 ms on the Swing thread, so the window stays responsive.
ball.intersects(paddle) is the rectangle collision check. java.awt.Rectangle does the overlap math for you.
super.paintComponent(g) clears the previous frame. Leaving it out draws a trail.
pitfall: Key presses do nothing if the panel does not have focus. Call setFocusable(true) on the panel. Also import javax.swing.Timer, not java.util.Timer, which runs on a different thread.
shot_note: Mid-game, after holding the Left key.
